Order-service's exhausted retries produced the api-gateway POST /checkout 503s with 6-26s latencies (#291, #293, #302). The gateway 503s are downstream symptoms. The small capacity dip was amplified by immediate non-backed-off retries, and the system did not recover because retry load stayed high. Ruled out: the postgres slow audit query (#254), the order-consumer GC pause (#279), and the gateway disk warning (#48), which are unrelated to the payment path.

The payment-svc v1.11.0 rollout at 08:19:55 coincided with onset. Instance draining and restoration (#280, #284) and the subsequent load spike could indicate the release reduced effective capacity or changed behavior. The logs show no explicit error from the new version itself, so this evidence is weaker than the retry amplification pattern.

Temporarily throttle checkout traffic at the gateway so payment-svc can drain its queue. Confirm the payment-svc v1.11.0 rollout reaches 4/4 capacity, and consider pausing or rolling back the deploy if drain/readiness is the cause. Add alerting on retry rate and inbound-to-baseline ratio.
